key_insight: A multi-domain EEG model combining spectral, connectivity, and topological features improved subject-level ADHD classification, with SVM performing best.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests a more informative, interpretable EEG-based approach for supporting ADHD research and future biomarker development, though it is not a clinical diagnostic tool.
method: 121-subject EEG dataset preprocessed into overlapping windows
Extracted 1,043 features across spectral, wPLI connectivity, and persistent homology domains
Applied recursive feature elimination and compared five classifiers with five-fold cross-validation
evidence_signal: Using stratified five-fold cross-validation, the top SVM model reached 80.17% accuracy, 80.95% F1-score, 86.72% ROC-AUC, and 87.34% PR-AUC.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated on a relatively small sample, so external validation on independent datasets is needed before broader use.
paper_title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification
